name: Mannheim Business School, University of Mannheim

class_size.note: 'Number of Participants: Up to 60'; class profile page says 50 to 60 per class

tuition_total.note: Includes course materials, IT, university services, extracurricular programmes and study-trip accommodation; excludes transport, accommodation and living costs in Mannheim. Early-bird discounts €3,000 (by 30 Nov 2026) or €1,000 (by 30 Apr); German language bonus €2,000; GMAT/GRE bonus €250

mandatory_fees_total.note: Non-refundable application fee €150; no other mandatory fee listed

living_budget_total.note: School FAQ: 'guideline total cost ... in the region of €15,000 - €17,000 for the whole program year' (accommodation €500-700/month, health insurance about €150/month for internationals, food and social €500-600/month). value = midpoint of the published range

scholarship.note: Seven scholarship categories; six of up to €6,000 (Growth & Scale, Finance, Consulting, German Excellence, Eastern Europe, Future Female Business Leader) and a need-based award up to €9,500. Can be combined with one early-bird discount and two bonuses. No average award published

employment.report_url_note: Full 'Employment Report for the Class of 2023' and 'Fast Track Report for the Class of 2024' are only available through a lead form (mbs.tfaforms.net); not submitted. Figures below are from the school's career page
employment.accepted_3m_note: Programme page: '95% accepted a job offer three months after graduating' (cohort not named); career page for Class of 2023: '93% accepted a job offer after graduation' (no time frame)

base_salary.note: 'Average post-MBA base salary: 110,264 USD', Class of 2023, career page

employment.changed_country_note: 97% switched country, function or industry; 42-43% made the triple change (country, role and industry); 93% now work in Germany (Class of 2023); 'more than 80% work in Germany after graduation' (programme page)
employment.by_industry_note: Only the ranking of the top 3 sectors is public; shares and salaries are in the gated report
employment.by_geography_note: 93% of the Class of 2023 work in Germany; no other region shares published on open pages
employment.top_employers_note: No employer list with hires on open pages

profile.note: 'On average 31 years of age and have already worked for seven or eight years' (7.5 = midpoint of the stated 7-8); 'nearly 40%' women. International share not stated in text; class profile charts are images (not read)

rankings_cited.note: School page: '#65 the Global MBA Ranking of the Financial Times (February 2026), #1 in Germany'

notes: Detailed industry/function/geography data and salary by sector are in a report gated by a lead form.
